items.title: Alice Zeno Interview, 1960-01-25
items.q: A while ago, Dave, before you came, we were speaking about the Indians...

ctx.x: Do you remember the names of any of the songs which came from Haiti or San Domingo, the Indians sang? I think some of the Creole songs undoubtedly came from Haiti. Yes. Because that's the language they speak, you know, Creole, it's Creole.

A while ago, Dave, before you came, we were speaking about the Indians and how they dressed. Yeah. And I was telling them children when I was in my teens that I would go to ball because we didn't, girls didn't run around like they do now. It was a pleasure then to look at the Indians. They were dressed like real Indians. They had that basket on the back, you know, and they sat on the floor and they'd eat the cowpies. I believe it was jambalaya. Jambalaya congri. It sat on the floor. But now the Indians, they've…
You want a Coke or anything? Yes, I like a Coke. You want a Coke? Yes. All right, if you have something. Maybe I'll take that instead of a Coke. I don't know. I don't drink that.
